overall: The AG found the Sept. 20 minutes sufficiently detailed and a concise summary of the Short Term Rental discussion, but violated the law by wrongly placing a member who had left the meeting in that discussion. It ordered amended minutes certified within 30 days and future compliance.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Sept. 20 minutes inaccurately summarized the Short Term Rental bylaw discussion and lacked detail on the rationale for the tenant sublet prohibition.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the minutes capture a concise summary of the Short Term Rental bylaw discussion even though they do not capture, at times, the exact statements.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Sept. 20 minutes were inaccurate; the AG found they named a member in the Short Term Rental discussion although he had left the meeting before that topic began.
allegations.key_passage: As such, we find that this statement in the minutes that references Mr. Reed does not accurately reflect the discussion that occurred.

allegations.summary: Not raised in the complaint: the AG, on its own review, noted inaccuracies in the Nov. 4 minutes (wrong meeting dates approved and a vote misreported) and urged revision.
allegations.key_passage: We strongly encourage the Subcommittee to revise the minutes of the November 4 meeting to accurately reflect the discussions and votes that actually occurred.

remedy: Amend the September 20 minutes to accurately reflect the discussion that occurred and certify to the AG within thirty (30) days that it has done so.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.
remedy_passage: We order the Board to amend the minutes of the September 20 meeting to accurately reflect the discussion that occurred and to certify to this office within thirty (30) days of the date of this letter that it has done so.
